issues.description: Field mismatch: Farm.animals collection type. The problem text (explicit instructions) requires Farm.animals to be a Set<Animal> and to be initialized with a new HashSet<>() in the no-argument constructor. The solution implementation declares private List<Animal> animals and initializes it with new ArrayList<>() (and the getter/setter use List<Animal>). This conflicts with the explicit requirement about uniqueness and the concrete collection type and may confuse students which collection to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Farm.animals field and its getter/setter in the solution to use Set<Animal> (e.g., private Set<Animal> animals;) and initialize it in the no-argument constructor with new HashSet<>(); update addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, and singFarmSong to operate on the Set. This makes the solution match the problem's requirement of unique animals and the specified concrete collection.

issues.description: Conflicting specification inside the problem statement for the Farm.animals attribute. The UML diagram lists Farm.animals as List<Animal>, while the textual instructions explicitly require a Set implemented as a HashSet (unique animals, initialize HashSet in the no-arg constructor). These two specifications (UML vs textual) disagree and create ambiguity for students about whether to implement animals as a List or a Set.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the problem statement: update the UML to show animals: Set<Animal> (and note HashSet as the intended implementation) so it matches the textual instructions. Alternatively, if a List is intended, change the textual instructions to require a List. Prefer making the UML match the textual instruction (Set/HashSet) to avoid ambiguity about uniqueness.
